summary: Open C headband copied from the user's moulded chain-link band: a curb chain of round oval wire links, slanted and twisted so each passes in front of the next, on a hidden solid spine along the inner face that makes the band stiffer (with see-through windows behind the links on the toothless arms), with two rows of grip teeth pointing at the head over the top arc and a smooth rounded pad at each tip. One piece, printed flat on the bed without supports (a hidden 50 deg keel under every wire, a 50 deg web under every tooth), in PETG (primary) and PLA.

inputs.notes: the user's words and stage 1 answers
top view, band lying flat on a cutting mat (1/2 inch grid, cm edge rulers); used for the outline sizes
low side view of the outer face: curb chain links, through openings, round end link
close-up of the inner face: two staggered rows of round pin teeth, about 2 per link per row
oblique top view: teeth run over the top arc only and stop above the widest point; the arms are plain chain

datum.origin: X = 0 on the band's mirror line (midway between the tips); Y = 0 at the outer face of the crown (top of the band); Z = 0 on the bed
datum.x: across the band, ear to ear, left to right seen from the front
datum.y: from the crown towards the tips (front = the crown's outer face, at -Y)
datum.z: up = print direction; the band lies flat, its height (D3) is the Z extent

print.orientation: flat on the bed as it lies on a table: the C shape in XY, band height in Z; layers run along the band, so bending it open never pulls layers apart; every tooth grows out of the spine on a 50 deg web, so nothing starts in mid-air

features.name: band centreline
features.position: two half-ellipses meeting at Y = D5: semi-axis X = D1/2 + D6/2 = 60.2 for both; upper vertical semi-axis D5 - D6/2 = 67.8 (crown centreline at Y 2.2); the lower half ends at the tips, X = ±(D4/2 + D6/2) = ±14.7, with the tip outer extreme at Y = D2
features.notes: symmetric about X = 0; the inner face of the body is D6/2 inside the centreline

features.name: curb chain links
features.position: centred on the centreline at the adjusted pitch (9.018), crown link at u = 0, from tip to tip
features.notes: 43 identical links. Each: an elliptical wire loop, D8 = 14 outer length, wire D27 = 2.4, its height filling D3 (wire centre half-axes 5.8 x 2.69), slanted D28 in the face and twisted D29 about Z, so its leading end passes in front of the next link and its trailing end behind: the curb / braid look. Neighbours overlap by D8 - D7 and fuse where the wires cross; the openings are open from the outside; behind them the spine (F5) is solid over the toothed zone and has a see-through window on the arms. Every wire carries a hidden D30 keel underneath; the lowest wire is cut flat D31 at the bed.

features.name: grip teeth
features.position: over D18 of centreline centred on the crown; per link 2 teeth D15 apart in each row; lower row at Z = D16, upper row at Z = D17, rows shifted D19 along the band; pointing inward along the centreline normal
features.notes: 76 teeth. Round pins (D13) with a rounded tip, rooted in the spine and pointing radially inward. Under each tooth a web, D13 wide with a D30 keel, whose lower edge climbs at D30 from the spine face (D14 x tan D30 = 3.0 below the tooth axis) to the tooth tip, so the tooth grows out of the spine layer by layer. The lower row's webs end on the bed.

features.name: tips
features.notes: each tip is a smooth rounded pad, D34 long, D6 thick and D3 high, round at the end and on the edges (radius D6/2); the last link runs into it; links and spine are trimmed inside the pad (all but its first 2 mm) so nothing pokes through

features.name: hidden spine
features.position: along the whole centreline, tip pad to tip pad; inner face flush with the band's inner face (D6/2 inside the centreline), extending D32 outward; Z 0 to D33
features.notes: solid wall with a round top and a keeled bottom cut by the bed, fused with every link; blends into each tip pad over 3 mm. It makes the band stiffer and carries the upper wires and teeth. On the arms, beyond the toothed zone, it has a see-through window behind every link's clear opening (20 in all, about 3.9 x 1.9): the window follows the opening D35 inside the wires, its floor is the material below, its top is flat for at most D36 (a short bridge) and slopes down at D30 beyond that. The toothed zone keeps a solid spine: each upper tooth's web stands on the spine right behind the link opening.

assumptions: A1: all outline sizes (D1, D2, D4, D5) are scaled from the top-view photo on the 1/2 inch mat grid (about ±3 mm); the user chose these over ruler measurements. The band flexes, so a few mm still fits; re-measure if the first print is too tight or loose.
A2: the mat grid is 1/2 inch (12.7 mm): the big numbers are inches, the edge rulers are cm (82-85 px/cm vs ~103 px per grid square in the display).

A3: rev 4: round interlocked links like the original, on a hidden spine. Over the toothed zone the openings are ~1.8 mm deep pockets; on the arms the spine has a see-through window behind each link (about a third of rev 3's clear opening). The spine stiffens the band and gives every wire and tooth something to grow from, so the slicer has nothing to support.
A4: the band is printed in its relaxed shape, the shape it has lying on the table in the photo.
A5: teeth are 1.4 thick instead of ~1.1 (user), round with a keel underneath and rounded tips.
A6: shape is mirror-symmetric about X = 0 (the photo shows the ends ~2 mm off centre: how it was lying); the link slant runs the same way along the whole band, as on a real chain.
A7: PETG is the primary material (flexes over the head); PLA is released too, but it is stiffer and can crack at the arms if opened wide.

A8: two printcheck warnings are accepted. Thin walls: the thin samples (z ~4.9) are the sharp edge of the hidden 50 deg keel under the upper wires, outside the spine, printed as a single line. Small hole: one 0.3 mm sliver gap between a wire and the spine on the left arm (x -37, y 131), thinner than one extrusion line; the slicer fills it. Layer alignment: a few short flat stretches of the sloped window floors (e.g. z 2.305) fall between layers; the slicer rounds them, harmless.

A9: stiffness: in the PETG band, opening it 17 mm per side (a 150 mm head) strains the spine about 0.7 % (PETG yields at about 4 %), roughly 1 N clamping per side. Infill barely changes this: the wires and spine are mostly perimeters. D32 is the stiffness setting.
